candidate.title: TCR-LA-MC / PCR
candidate.scope: Assigned lower poster row: TCR ligation-anchored-magnetically captured PCR, ending in the depicted indexed Illumina P5/P7 library. The two title fragments TCR-LA-MC and PCR form one method name. The matching page 104 heading and schematic confirm this scope. The generic chain drawing represents recovery of α- or β-chain TCR sequences; it does not depict pooling or pairing of those chains. The adjacent TCR Chain Pairing/oil-emulsion row, cropped upper-row labels, right-hand locked-nucleic-acid legend, and bottom bibliography for other assays are context. Embedded ligation and PCR components, the paper’s 454 implementation, RACE comparisons, and unshown adaptations are not additional target workflows. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete experimental protocol. The paper’s main amplification implementation resolves the compressed transition from PCR 1 to PCR 2 through recapture and release of non-biotinylated strands. This is distinct from comparative variants in that paper that omit this capture or add adapters directly during PCR 2.

For TCR analysis, RNA was used as the starting material and gene-specific cDNA synthesis was performed using a biotinylated primer located in the constant (C) gene of the TCR chains. The resulting full-length cDNA fragments were magnetically captured on streptavidin beads and ligated to a known single-stranded linker cassette (ssLC). After exponential PCR amplification, sequencing adaptors were added and the PCR products were deep sequenced.
Biotinylated fragments originated during the cDNA synthesis were captured on streptavidin magnetic beads (Life Technologies).
evidence.rationale: The chemical selection recognizes biotin. The paper’s additional specificity-enhancing capture shows that capture is an enrichment operation, not evidence that every retained fragment is a biologically correct TCR target.

operations.label: ssDNA linker ligation
operations.description: Covalently joins the ssLC to the exposed cDNA 3′ end, creating a known sequence on the rearranged-region side of the bead-attached template.

operations.information_effect: Adds a common PCR priming site opposite the known C-gene site, so the intervening rearranged TCR sequence can be amplified.
